noveltyJustification: First evidence pass: 3 fully new gaps (repo-reuse rung, ladder-local never-cut guardrail, pre-write reach enumeration), 3 partially new, 3 confirmations of already-adopted doctrine.
keyQuestions: What is Ponytail 5.1.0's core doctrine, cost model, and smallest-complete-change ladder, and which parts are absent from the sk-code parent hub and its modes?
answeredQuestions: What is Ponytail 5.1.0's core doctrine, cost model, and smallest-complete-change ladder, and which parts are absent from the sk-code parent hub and its modes?

graphEvents.label: Repo-reuse rung absent from sk-code ladder

label: Ponytail 5's ladder keeps a rung-2 reuse-what-is-already-in-the-codebase step that sk-code's transplanted ladder omits; the date-picker example shows the intended behavior. Classification: NEW.

Ponytail pairs the ladder with an explicit never-cut list (trust-boundary validation, data-loss handling, security, accessibility, calibration); the sk-code ladder section carries no local guardrail even though P0/P1/P2 tiers own the floors elsewhere. Classification: NEW (localization gap).

Ponytail's 'lazy code without its check is unfinished' reflex (one small test or assert-based self-check for non-trivial logic) has no sk-code-packet phrasing; the framework AGENTS.md 'Test what changed' rule is the only coverage. Classification: NEW (packet-local).
Ponytail's one-line reply close (what was skipped, what risk) is already covered by sk-code verification's blind-spot reporting and the framework close-out mandate. Classification: ALREADY-ADOPTED.

Ponytail enumerates the change's full reach before editing (callers, tests, fixtures, config, exports); sk-code's implement doctrine names only conventions, callers, and examples. Classification: NEW (narrower enumeration).

Ponytail's one-prompt-many-hosts structure vs sk-code's hub-plus-nested-packets structure: sk-code's structure is the stronger fit for multi-mode scope, and the prior refinement already rejected per-host copies and always-on injection. Classification: ALREADY-ADOPTED (divergence by design).

Ponytail's lite/full/ultra intensity levels stay rejected as a verification slider; the adopted remnant is the SK_CODE_REVIEW_DEPTH alias that only names an existing tier. Classification: ALREADY-ADOPTED.

Ponytail's published restraint deltas (code/time/cost/tokens) and test-rate counter-claim belong in sk-code's benchmark harness as supporting metrics, never as severity gates; prior research already allowed the benchmark-only variant. Classification: NEW (harness-scoped).
Ponytail's shortcut comment form already landed as neutral ceiling content, banned brand prefixes, and an explicit allowlist exclusion. Classification: ALREADY-ADOPTED.
